en.title: The Longue Durée of Migration
en.summary: Migration is not a late disturbance imposed on a formerly immobile society. Across Mithila, Vajji, Anga and the adjoining Nepal plains, mobility has repeatedly connected household survival, scholarship, pilgrimage, military and administrative service, trade, marriage, cultivation and wage labour. What changed over the longue durée was not the existence of movement but its scale, duration, destinations, transport technologies, labour regimes and relationship to household reproduction.

mai.title: प्रवासनक दीर्घकालिक इतिहास
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “प्रवासनक दीर्घकालिक इतिहास” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Migration must be treated as a recurrent social institution, not as an exceptional crisis
A longue-durée history requires a vocabulary broader than the modern census category of migrant
River corridors made mobility structural long before railways
Early historic towns and religious institutions created circuits of travel without implying mass labour migration

en.title: Calcutta/Kolkata and Mithila–Anga Migration
en.summary: Calcutta was one of the first great external cities to become woven into the ordinary reproduction of households in Mithila, Vajji and Anga. The connection did not arise from one recruitment drive or one industry. It accumulated through river traffic, the East India Company capital, railways, jute mills, docks, warehouses, carts and rickshaws, construction, domestic and hotel service, petty trade, clerical work and later professional employment.

mai.title: कलकत्ता/कोलकाता आ मिथिला-अंग प्रवासन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “कलकत्ता/कोलकाता आ मिथिला-अंग प्रवासन” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Calcutta became an extension of village economies before it became a permanent destination for many migrants
The colonial capital created labour demand well beyond the factory gate
Jute industrialisation transformed the scale of the eastward labour corridor
Railways converted a difficult journey into a reproducible migration route

en.title: Delhi, Mumbai and Post-Independence Mobility
en.summary: After independence, migration from Mithila, Vajji and Anga ceased to be organised mainly around a small number of older eastern corridors. Calcutta/Kolkata remained important, but Delhi and Mumbai entered household migration strategies with growing force. The two metropolitan systems were not interchangeable. Delhi was closer by rail, located within the broad Hindi linguistic zone and increasingly surrounded by a National Capital Region of construction sites, workshops, warehouses and service jobs.

mai.title: दिल्ली, मुम्बई आ स्वतन्त्रताक बादक गतिशीलता
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “दिल्ली, मुम्बई आ स्वतन्त्रताक बादक गतिशीलता” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Post-independence migration widened the metropolitan map rather than replacing older corridors
Delhi’s expansion after 1947 created an unusually large and varied demand for labour
Rail accessibility and the broad Hindi environment lowered some barriers to entry into Delhi
Delhi gradually became a regional labour market extending far beyond the municipal core

en.title: Punjab, Haryana and Seasonal Agricultural Labour
en.summary: The migration of agricultural labour from Bihar to Punjab and Haryana is one of the clearest examples of how India’s uneven regional development created a labour market across distant rural worlds. The corridor did not arise because rural people suddenly abandoned agriculture for the city. It grew because the Green Revolution intensified farming in north-western India at the same time that large parts of eastern India continued to contain small holdings, irregular employment and lower cash wages.

mai.title: पंजाब, हरियाणा आ मौसमी कृषिश्रम
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “पंजाब, हरियाणा आ मौसमी कृषिश्रम” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The Green Revolution created a new rural-to-rural migration corridor
The expansion of paddy made transplanting the decisive labour bottleneck
Eastern Bihar supplied workers because the wage gap intersected with underemployment
Railways turned a distant opportunity into a repeatable journey

en.title: Nepal–India Circular Migration
en.summary: The India–Nepal border is international in law but unusually permeable in everyday social life. In the Mithila–Madhesh and Anga-facing borderlands, households have long treated the line not only as a frontier of two states but also as a corridor linking labour markets, marriage fields, pilgrimages, schools, hospitals, bazaars and transport nodes.

mai.title: नेपाल-भारत परिपत्र प्रवासन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “नेपाल-भारत परिपत्र प्रवासन” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The border divided sovereignty without severing a social region
The 1950 Treaty gave reciprocal mobility a durable interstate framework
Open-border migration is systematically undercounted
Circularity is produced by low travel costs and the possibility of return

en.title: Gulf Migration
en.summary: Gulf migration extended the mobility repertoire of Mithila, Vajji and Anga beyond the internal corridors described in Chapters 97–101. From the oil-boom decades onward, employment in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain offered a different combination of distance, earnings, risk and household strategy. The journey demanded passports, visas, contracts, recruitment payments and air travel rather than the railway ticket and village contact that often organised internal migration.

mai.title: खाड़ी प्रवासन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “खाड़ी प्रवासन” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The oil boom opened a new labour frontier
Internal migration provided much of the social infrastructure for overseas mobility
Overseas work raised the entry cost of migration
Recruitment chains connect village information to foreign employers

en.title: Remittances and Household Transformation
en.summary: Migration changes a household only when earnings are converted into transfers, decisions and assets. A remittance is therefore more than money crossing distance. It is the mechanism by which labour performed in Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai, Punjab, the Nepal–India corridor or the Gulf enters the food budget, school fees, medical treatment, debt ledger, house, field, marriage account and savings decisions of a household in Mithila, Vajji, Anga or Madhesh.

mai.title: विप्रेषण आ घरेलू रूपान्तरण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “विप्रेषण आ घरेलू रूपान्तरण” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Remittances turn individual mobility into a household economic institution
Gross earnings, remitted money and household gain are three different quantities
Internal and international remittances belong to the same household portfolio but have different rhythms
Older Bihar data show that remittances were already a major component of recipient household expenditure

en.title: Urbanisation
en.summary: Urbanisation in Mithila, Vajji and Anga is not adequately described by the growth of a few municipal populations. It is a transformation of the settlement system: villages acquire markets, schools, clinics, banks, transport stands and non-farm employment; district headquarters extend into peri-urban fringes; railway and highway corridors generate ribbon development; remittance-funded houses alter land use; and people commute daily between places that remain administratively ‘rural’ and places legally designated…

mai.title: नगरीकरण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “नगरीकरण” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Urbanisation is a change in the settlement system, not merely migration to a city
Bihar’s measured urban share remained exceptionally low through the 2011 Census
The legal definition of a town influences the historical record
Bihar’s urban population multiplied faster than its urban share

en.title: Informal Economies and Street Commerce
en.summary: The streets, station approaches, haats, bus stands, hospital gates, school corridors, neighbourhood crossings and peri-urban roads of Mithila, Vajji and Anga sustain a dense economy that conventional city histories often understate. Street vending is only its most visible layer.

mai.title: अनौपचारिक अर्थव्यवस्था आ सड़क-बजार
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “अनौपचारिक अर्थव्यवस्था आ सड़क-बजार” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Informality is an institutional relationship, not a synonym for illegality
Periodic haats form the deep historical infrastructure beneath modern street commerce
Street commerce converts footfall into a productive asset
Low fixed costs make petty trade an entry point for migrants and households with little capital

en.title: Diaspora Cultural Institutions
en.summary: Migration does not automatically create a diaspora community. People may share an origin yet remain dispersed across workplaces, neighbourhoods, languages, classes and generations. A cultural institution is one of the mechanisms that converts this dispersion into a recurring public: an association, literary circle, festival committee, religious or welfare group, arts collective, publication, digital forum, student network or community centre that gives regular form to belonging.

mai.title: प्रवासी सांस्कृतिक संस्थान
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “प्रवासी सांस्कृतिक संस्थान” विषयक दीर्घकालिक प्रवासन, महानगरीय आ खाड़ी गतिशीलता, विप्रेषण, नगरीकरण आ प्रवासी संस्थानक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Diaspora begins as dispersion; institutions create the recurring public that makes diaspora durable
Kolkata, industrial towns and Delhi formed important institutional environments for twentieth-century Maithil mobility
The association occupies a middle level between household intimacy and state recognition
Vidyapati Parva became a portable public form through which Maithili cultural identity could be staged away from home
